content_metadata.description: A demonstration of the Planetroid app, which shows the positions of planets around the Sun.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the app being demonstrated?
Which planet is seen popping in when the person shifts the view to the side?
What year is the simulation set to when the person stops time for the first time?

qAndA.answer: The person mentions adding the ability to click a planet and track it, as well as controlling the speed and jumping to specific dates.
qAndA.question: What are some improvements planned for the app?

activities.description: The person introduces Planetroid, an app that shows the positions of the planets around the Sun.
The person launches the Planetroid app.
The person moves the angle of the screen to view the planets from the side.
The person zooms in to get a closer look at the planets.
The person stops the time simulation.
The person shifts the screen around and zooms in to get a closer look at the Earth.
The person plays the time simulation forward and then backward.

https://market.android.com/details?id=com.codepraxis.orrery

App that lets you see the positions of the planets around the sun based on date. Plays forwards and backwards. Just like the ancient orrery devices!
